meaning: to raise petty or trivial objections to something
sentence: He would cavil at the wording of every clause instead of signing the contract.

meaning: persistently fault-finding over trifles, or the habit of making such petty objections
sentence: His caviling tone wore the committee down long before the vote was taken.

meaning: to cut out parts of a book, film or letter thought objectionable, or the official who does so
sentence: The wartime censor struck out every reference to troop movements.

meaning: a grain such as wheat, rice or maize grown for food, or a breakfast food made from it
sentence: Wheat is the chief cereal grown across the northern plains.

meaning: having a compelling personal charm that inspires devotion in others
sentence: The charismatic commander could hold a whole parade ground in silence.

meaning: forming or leading up to the most intense and decisive point of a series of events
sentence: The climactic charge on the ridge decided the whole battle.

meaning: relating to climate, the long-term weather conditions of a region
sentence: Climatic conditions in the desert allow only a few hardy crops.

meaning: behaving in a foolish or comically awkward way
sentence: His clownish antics at the mess dinner embarrassed the senior officers.

meaning: awkwardness in movement or handling, or a lack of tact in dealing with people
sentence: His clumsiness with the rifle bolt cost him marks on the firing range.

meaning: upright pillars supporting a structure, vertical divisions of a page or table of figures, or troops moving one behind another
sentence: The columns of the old veranda were each carved from a single block of stone.

meaning: to examine two or more things in order to note their likenesses and differences
sentence: Compare the two maps and you will see that the river has shifted course.

meaning: the person who introduces the performers in a variety show, or to act as such a host
sentence: She agreed to compere the annual cultural night at the academy.

meaning: the party who lays a formal charge or brings a complaint before a court
sentence: The complainant told the magistrate that his shop had been looted.

meaning: a willingness to oblige others and fall in with their wishes
sentence: His complaisance made him popular but left him with no opinions of his own.

meaning: to grasp the meaning of something, or to take something in within its scope
sentence: It took him a while to comprehend the gravity of the order.

meaning: agreement and harmony between people or states, or a formal treaty recording it
sentence: The two neighbouring villages have lived in concord for generations.

meaning: of a punishment, fitting and thoroughly deserved
sentence: The court thought a long sentence condign for so cold a crime.

meaning: a person trusted with one's private affairs and secrets
sentence: The old colonel was his only confidant in the regiment.

meaning: present from birth, and loosely, so deep-seated as to seem inborn
sentence: The child was treated for a congenital heart defect.

meaning: relating to marriage or to the relationship between husband and wife
sentence: The prisoner applied for conjugal visits during his term.

meaning: descended from a common ancestor and so related by blood
sentence: The two families are consanguine, tracing a common great-grandfather.

meaning: the inner sense of right and wrong that governs a person's conduct
sentence: His conscience would not let him keep the money he had found.

meaning: awake and aware of one's surroundings, or done deliberately and with awareness
sentence: She remained conscious throughout the operation.

meaning: to plot secretly with others to do something unlawful, or of events, to combine towards one result
sentence: Two clerks conspired to alter the muster roll.

meaning: existing or happening during the same period of time
sentence: The two inscriptions are contemporaneous, both cut in the fifth century.

meaning: sharing a common boundary, so that the two things touch or adjoin
sentence: Their fields are contiguous, divided only by a low bund.

meaning: dependent on something else that may or may not happen, or a group forming part of a larger body
sentence: The bonus is contingent on the unit meeting its target.

meaning: cheerful and friendly, fond of good company and festivity
sentence: The mess was a convivial place on a Saturday evening.

meaning: so complicated and twisted as to be hard to follow
sentence: His convoluted explanation left the board more puzzled than before.

meaning: clever at getting what one wants by cunning or deceit
sentence: A crafty broker sold him the same plot twice.

meaning: contemptibly cowardly, lacking the least courage
sentence: His craven retreat left the flank wide open.

meaning: by way of a total built up from successive additions, taken all together
sentence: Cumulatively, the small fines came to more than a month's pay.
